⭐ 1-Star Review — Motorola Edge 70 Fusion
Very disappointed with the durability and after-sales support.

I purchased the Motorola Edge 70 Fusion (Pantone Silhouette, 256 GB) from Flipkart, and I am extremely disappointed with the build quality.
The phone accidentally fell from a height of less than 2 feet, and the display got cracked/damaged. This is especially disappointing because the phone is marketed with Tough Gorilla Glass protection. For a phone in this price range, I expected much better durability.
What makes the situation even worse is the service center experience. I approached the service center regarding the damaged glass, but they informed me that they do not provide glass-only replacement and that the complete display assembly needs to be replaced. This makes a minor accidental drop unnecessarily expensive.

I am attaching the photo showing the cracked display as evidence.
Motorola should seriously look into both the durability of the display protection and the availability of glass-only replacement. A phone advertised with Tough Gorilla Glass should offer better protection against such a small fall, and customers should have a more reasonable repair option.

Very sleek and elegant looking. Extremely comfortable to hold due to the Rounder Corners and Curved Edge. Feels premium, durable to hold. 

After a day of settling down performance and experience is smooth despite me having over 300 apps installed and a ton of them sending me regular notifications and updates. 

Multimedia experience is incredible. Screen is bright and has incredible colours without being inaccurate and super contrasty. Speakers are some of the best I've ever heard on a phone. Loud but Clean and Crisp. You can literally feel the Bass through the phone It's that powerful but it isn't the Rough kinda Base that no one likes, it's Crisp and Well-Controlled. 

The battery is absolutely incredible, where my last phone (120 Hz screen 500 Mah Redmi) would go from 100 to 0 in 6 hrs of SOT, this phone didn't even feel 50%.

Software is pretty good but not as feature-ful as some other Android Skins (Though I knew this beforehand and wanted the Clean Experience). I switched to a different launcher as the Moto one is a bit too undercooked. Hopefully they improve the Launcher with future OS Updates. Also some apps that are poorly coded (Gov apps Bank apps(often Hitch and Lag on Startup) which I see on pretty much every Android Skin except Samsung OneUI so I hope Moto looks at Samsung's OneUI and figure out how to make HelloUI just as Smooth even with Gov/Bank and other poorly coded apps. 

The Camera setup is probably the best overall you can get in the 25K price Bracket right now. Maybe not Individually the best each but the Rear, Rear Ultrawide and the Front all products great results for the price and when combined it provides a great well-balanced experience. It's missing a Telephoto but imo going above 5x Zoom is a gimmick and 99.9% of users would only ever have the need for such a thing rarely.

Phone is having lot of problems Within 1–2 weeks of purchase, the device started developing recurring issues that continue to occur intermittently:

During calls, I am unable to hear the other person, and calls disconnect automatically even after changing the SIM.
The phone unexpectedly reboots on its own, shows the Motorola logo, freezes, and resumes only after some time.
When manually restarting, it sometimes remains completely switched off and takes 5–10 minutes before restarting.
The camera occasionally captures blank photos despite sufficient storage being available.

I am a working professional, and this phone contains important work-related applications. These unpredictable failures can occur during working hours and directly affect my productivity and reliability at work. It is not practical to wait for the issue to happen and rush to a service centre simply to demonstrate an intermittent fault.

The combination of audio failure, random rebooting, freezing, restart failure, and blank camera output raises concern about a possible hardware or manufacturing defect, rather than a normal isolated software issue. I request your senior technical team to investigate the device comprehensively and advise the root cause.

Overall, the phone offers a good and balanced experience. The design looks really good and feels premium. The performance is good, the display quality is impressive, and the software experience is smooth.

The charging speed is okay, but it is not as fast as I expected. Heating is manageable and not a major issue during normal use.

However, the worst part of the phone is the camera quality. Compared with Samsung phones in the same price range, Samsung offers much better picture quality, especially in terms of colors, details, and overall image processing. Motorola definitely needs to improve its camera performance.

Overall, it is a good phone with a great design, good performance, display, and software, but the camera quality is the biggest disappointment.
